Add content pages to document

Source: R/pipe-composition.R
rtf_tables.Rd

Append one or more content items as pages. Each element of tables becomes exactly one page, holding a single table or figure.

Usage

rtf_tables(
  doc,
  tables,
  col_header = NULL,
  col_header_align = NULL,
  spanning_header = NULL,
  col_spec = NULL,
  row_title = NULL,
  border = "tfl",
  blank_rows = NULL,
  read_attributes = TRUE,
  style = NULL,
  col_rel_width = NULL,
  column_widths_twips = NULL,
  table_width_twips = NULL,
  table_width_pct_of_writable = NULL,
  table_width_pct = NULL,
  table_align = "left",
  row_height_twips = NULL,
  row_height_exact = FALSE,
  header_row_height_twips = NULL,
  blank_row_height_twips = NULL,
  cell_padding_left_twips = NULL,
  cell_padding_right_twips = NULL,
  cell_valign = "bottom",
  blank_row_normalize = c("detect", "collapse"),
  markup = NULL,
  font_size_half_points = NULL,
  font = NULL,
  titles = NULL,
  footnotes = NULL,
  auto_section = NULL,
  section_label_align = "left",
  auto_title = NULL,
  title_label_align = "left",
  read_gt = FALSE,
  page_break = TRUE,
  first_rows = NULL,
  space_before = 0L,
  cont_title = NULL
)

Arguments

doc

An rtf_document object.

tables

The pages to add. The usual forms are:

a table_plan

(from table_plan()) the plan of an ARD or a data.frame; it becomes its pages, as plan_apply() would make them.

the output of as_rtftables()

the pages of a gt, gtsummary, rtables/tern, rlistings, flextable or huxtable table, or of a data.frame paged and styled there.

a bare data.frame

one simple page; the table-format arguments below apply to it.

More generally, tables is one page or a list of pages, each element one page with a single content: a data.frame, an rtftable (from rtftable() or as_rtftables()), an rtfplot (from rtfplot()), or a gt_tbl / gtsummary table. A gt_tbl or gtsummary table is best passed through as_rtftables(), which reads its labels, alignment, titles and source notes; placed here directly it is treated like a data.frame unless read_gt is set (see read_gt).

tables may also be a single object of a class another package has registered an as_rtftables() method for; it is converted to its pages first (see "Supplying a source from another package" in as_rtftables()).

col_header, col_header_align, spanning_header, col_spec, row_title, border, blank_rows, read_attributes, style, col_rel_width, column_widths_twips, table_width_twips, table_width_pct_of_writable, table_width_pct, table_align, row_height_twips, row_height_exact, header_row_height_twips, blank_row_height_twips, cell_padding_left_twips, cell_padding_right_twips, cell_valign, blank_row_normalize, markup, font_size_half_points, font

Deprecated (removed in 0.9.0): the same arguments of rtftable(), written there (or in as_rtftables() / plan_style()) instead. See "Deprecated arguments" below.

titles

NULL (default) or a list of length length(tables) or length 1 (a single block applied to every page). Each element is a title block: either a character vector (one entry per row, default styling) or a list of rows, where a row is a string or a styled list(text=, align=, bold=, italic=, underline=, color=, border=). An empty string ("") is a blank row. The block renders as a single-column table the same width as the content (so it lines up); title rows default to centred + bold.

Title and footnote text may carry the same page-number tokens as a header or footer band – {AUTO_PAGE}, {AUTO_TOTAL_PAGES}, {PAGE}, {TOTAL_PAGES} – which is how a per-table "Page 1 of 3" sits next to the table instead of at the page margin. A static {PAGE} costs nothing here: these bands are re-emitted for every page, so each page bakes its own number without the extra RTF section the same token forces in a header. A table paginated on a column fills {<column name>} with its page's value (see Page values).

footnotes

NULL (default) or a list of length length(tables) or length 1 (common to all). Same block structure as titles, and the same page-number tokens; footnote rows default to left-aligned, and the first row carries a top rule (the separator) unless that row sets its own border.

auto_section

Logical. When TRUE and tables is a named list, each name is used as a per-section heading appended to the common header defined by rtf_section(secinfo = ...) (called without a page argument). A section opens where the name changes, so a run of pages carrying the same name – the pages of one split table, which all share its heading – is one section of several pages. A "...n" tail (the serial as_rtftables() adds so a page list with repeated headings stays addressable by name) is not part of the name here: it is stripped before both the comparison and the printed heading. An item with an empty name falls through into the open section, which is how pages whose headings differ are put in one section (see combine_sections()). NULL (default): what the pages say — a plan's plan_paginate_group(heading_at = "section") — else FALSE.

section_label_align

Alignment for the auto-appended section label row. One of "left" (default), "center", or "right".

auto_title

Logical. When TRUE and tables is a named list, each name is appended as the last row of that table's title block, so it prints immediately above the table rather than in the page header. Titles already present – from titles =, or carried on the object as the rtf_titles attribute by as_rtftables() – are kept and the name goes after them; a table with no titles gets the name as its whole block. Unnamed items are untouched. Behaves identically under either title_format. Composes with auto_section, which puts the same name in the section header instead. NULL (default): what the pages say — a plan's plan_paginate_group(heading_at = "title") — else FALSE.

title_label_align

Alignment for the auto-appended title label row. One of "left" (default), "center", or "right".

read_gt

Deprecated (removed in 0.9.0): pass a gt or gtsummary table through as_rtftables(), which reads its labels, alignment, titles and source notes, and place the pages it returns here.

page_break

TRUE (the default): each table begins a new page. FALSE: a table goes on under the content before it, on the page that one ends on – a listing under its summary table. Nothing is measured: what does not fit, the reader (Word, LibreOffice) carries to the next page by itself – with no title, no column header and no footnote there; fitting the page is the program's to arrange. To go on with the title, column header and footnote on pages of its own, give first_rows. One value for every table, or one each. A table's own later pages (a plan's, or as_rtftables()'s) always begin a page; so does the document's first content. Unlike reporter's add_content(page_break = ) this is the break before the table. A page has one auto_section heading: that of the first table on it that has one; a later table on the page with another heading gets a warning (auto_title names it on its title), and no page break is added for it. The page header and footer are the section's; a static {PAGE} / {TOTAL_PAGES} counts the pages as written, which are right when each page holds what fits it: the program counts the rows. rtf_section()(page = n) counts the pages as written; rtf_layout() shows them.

first_rows

With page_break = FALSE, the rows of the table that go on the page before it; the rest is paginated as the table says – a plan's plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = , split = ) – each page with its title, column header and footnote. The program counts what fits: rtfreporter does not measure the page. tables is then one table: a table_plan(), a data frame (its rest one page; for max_rows give as_rtftables()(first_rows = ) the pages) or an rtftable() (cut there, its rest one page). NULL (the default): the whole table goes on.

space_before

With page_break = FALSE, empty lines between the content before and this table (0: the title's own blank line alone).

cont_title

A line under the title of each later page of a table ("(continued)"): the pages after the shared one of first_rows, and a table's own later pages (a plan's, or as_rtftables()'s max_rows pages). NULL: none. rtf_titles() replaces the titles whole, this line too. Not as_rtftables()'s cont_label, which marks a group cut across pages.

Value

Modified rtf_document with appended contents.

Details

A table's appearance is written where the table is made: in rtftable(), as_rtftables() or plan_style(). A bare data.frame placed here gets their defaults.

Page values

A table cut into pages on a column – as_rtftables()(page_by = ), a value split on a named group column (split = "by_value", group_col = ), a plan's plan_paginate_group() – knows each page's value of that column. A title, footnote, auto_section heading, header or footer (rtf_header() / rtf_footer()) then writes {<column name>} ({PARAM}, {SEX}) and gets that page's value when the file is written:

  • a title or footnote takes the value of its own table, so on a page of several tables (page_break = FALSE) each names its own;

  • a header or footer belongs to the page: each column takes the first table on the page with a value for it (the rule of the auto_section heading); a later table with another value gets a warning. A band that uses one is written for each page, as one with a static {PAGE} is;

  • a {NAME} the page has no value for is printed as written, as any unknown token is (a title's {N} stays {N}); rtfreporter's own tokens ({PAGE}, {PROGRAM}, ...) and a token of one's own (rtf_document(tokens = )) of the same name win over a column's.

The values are on each page's rtf_paginate_meta as page_values (c(PARAM = "ALT")), and rtf_layout() shows them. An rtables page from rtables::paginate_table() carries its split_rows_by(page_by = TRUE) values by their page-title prefix; a gt_group member of tfrmt's print_to_gt() the page_structure() columns of a page_plan(note_loc = ) that writes the page note.

Deprecated arguments

The 26 table-format arguments that copy rtftable()'s (col_header, border, col_rel_width, row_height_twips, font_size_half_points, font, ... – see the usage) and read_gt are deprecated in 0.8.x: each one passed says so once a session and still works as before, and they are removed in 0.9.0, the first CRAN release. Write the same settings on the table: rtftable(df, border = "tfl", col_rel_width = c(2, 1)), or as_rtftables(x, ...) for a paged or converted table; pass a gt or gtsummary table through as_rtftables() instead of read_gt. Until then they behave as they always did: used to build a bare data.frame element, and, when passed explicitly, overriding the matching field of a pre-built rtftable() page (rtfplot() pages are never modified).

Examples

# Two clinical tables in one document, each on its own page with its own
# title; each table carries its own appearance (rtftable()), and a footnote
# is attached to the first page only.
t1 <- data.frame(Parameter = c("Age (years)", "Sex, n (%)"),
                 Value = c("75.1 (8.2)", "120 (53%)"))
t2 <- data.frame(Parameter = c("Weight (kg)", "Height (cm)"),
                 Value = c("78.0 (12.1)", "170 (9.5)"))

doc <- rtf_document() |>
  rtf_section(page = 1, secinfo = list(header = NULL, footer = NULL)) |>
  rtf_tables(
    list(rtftable(t1, border = "tfl", col_rel_width = c(2, 1)),
         rtftable(t2, border = "tfl", col_rel_width = c(2, 1))),
    titles    = list("Table 14.1.1", "Table 14.1.2"),
    footnotes = list("Source: ADSL", NULL)
  )
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".rtf")
generate_rtfreport(doc, f)
unlink(f)
